inputs.original_text: A jury in Wisconsin has found a man guilty of election fraud and identity theft for requesting the ballots of Republican state Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Democratic Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. A Racine County jury on Tuesday found Harry Wait guilty of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge following a two-day trial. He was acquitted of a second count of identity theft. Wait leads a group that makes false election claims. He admitted in 2022 that he requested the ballots to try to prove that the state’s voter registration system is vulnerable to fraud.
inputs.modified_text: They’re turning Harry Wait into the story so nobody has to confront what he was trying to expose: he requested ballots in the names of Robin Vos and Cory Mason to demonstrate that Wisconsin’s voter registration system could be exploited. The jury convicted him on two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge, while acquitting him of a second identity theft count. That split outcome lets officials claim the system is secure while punishing someone who tested it. The trial looks less like a warning about election vulnerabilities than a message about what happens when you make those vulnerabilities visible.
